title: OpenAI in early talks for a $1.2–$1.5 trillion funding round
subtitle: Reports this week say investors have approached OpenAI about a private round that would more than double the $852 billion valuation set in March.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: OpenAI is in early-stage talks with investors about a private funding round that would value the company between $1.2 trillion and $1.5 trillion, according to reports from the Financial Times and The Information surfaced this week. The outreach came from potential backers rather than OpenAI itself, and no round has been formalized. The target would more than double the $852 billion valuation set in the March 2026 round that raised $122 billion. CEO Sam Altman has publicly said an IPO will not happen in 2026. Reported annualized revenue surpassed $40 billion in July.

A trillion-dollar-plus private valuation moves OpenAI into territory shared with only a handful of public companies. Doing it before going public tells you two things. Investors treat compute and energy spend as a one-way ratchet — the money raised here is largely earmarked for data centers, chips, grid deals, research, and talent. And they still prefer a private cap table where disclosure requirements are thinner. The gap between this private-market number and the eventual IPO price is where either confirmation or correction will land.

The talks follow a stacked few months — Microsoft's expanded partnership, the Oracle and We Energies nuclear deal in Wisconsin, the Ironclad contract-agents partnership, and the expanded Atlassian deal that brings GPT-6 Astra into Jira and Confluence. They also arrive against a run of safety-team departures and the FTC's broad consumer-protection investigation of frontier labs, which together make the political cost of a trillion-dollar round harder to ignore.

Early-stage talks are not deals. The valuation that lands often diverges from the one leaked — sometimes by double digits in either direction. When you read a trillion-dollar headline, the single most useful question is who is doing the valuing, and whether anyone has written a check at that number yet. The answer here, for now, is nobody.
